correctness.rationale: Solving \(ab+c=a!+c!\) gives the unique base \(b=(a-1)!+(c!-c)/a\) and integrality condition \(a\mid(c!-c)\). The four cases partition \(c=0\), \(c\in\{1,2\}\), and \(c\ge3\) according to \(a\le c\) or \(a>c\). Digit bounds are checked exactly, with \((3,3)\) the sole failure in the \(a\le c\) divisibility branch. The divisor-count corollary is then immediate. Two independent finite replay modes agree.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-base literature already highlights two-digit infinite factorion constructions, so classifying the whole two-digit stratum is a motivated structural gap. The theorem gives a unique forced-base normal form, proves every leading digit occurs infinitely often, and provides an exact divisor count for every fixed trailing digit \(c\ge4\).
